title: GSC VM semantics measured in the game's own VM
description: One game's script VM behaviours (scheduling, notify, endon, waits, value semantics, name resolution at load), each measured by running one of this project's own conformance scripts in the game's VM emulated offline from the executable. Validates semantics/<engine-id>.toml after TOML parsing. Facts only: questions, one-sentence answers, the traces our own scripts produce, and the engine's short messages; no game code, no script text of the game.

extractor.description: The gruff script that ran the suite.

dump.description: Executable file name and its sha256, never a path.

suite.description: The folder of the conformance scripts in gruff.

time_unit.description: What the f<n> stamp of a trace line counts.

modes.description: The VM modes the suite ran in; the first is the one `trace` records.

id.description: The conformance script's file name, without .gsc.

answer.description: The fact, in one sentence. Required unless result is unsupported.

result.description: pass: the trace is the golden (or the compiler's refusal is the answer to a name-resolution question about a well-formed script: compile_error, no trace); unsupported: run and recorded, not judged: the form the behaviour is about cannot exist in the game (its compiler refuses the script: compile_error records the message) or the harness cannot vouch for the result (see reason). A failing test is never written here.

trace.description: Golden trace lines: f<time> T<thread> <logprint text | script error...>.

error.description: How the run ended when it did not end by itself: a load failure, Com_Error, or a harness limit.

compile_error.description: The game's (or the official) compiler's message when it refuses the script. On an unsupported behaviour: the form under test does not exist in the game. On a passing one: the refusal is the answer (a threaded call or a function reference that never reaches a builtin).

developer_trace.description: The developer-mode trace (first lines), when it differs.

alt_trace.description: The trace of the second mode of meta.modes when it is not a developer mode (T8: script errors continue), when it differs.

modes_agree.description: The two runs of meta.modes (retail and developer, or the game's own pair) gave the same trace and error.

dialect.description: The same question asked of another game's VM (its semantics file): whether this game's answer is the same.

note.description: The other game's answer when it differs, or what it lacks.

evidence.description: The second measure: a static reading of the handler or function that decides the behaviour (RVAs of this dump).

source.description: A source id of sources.toml, optionally #fragment.

agrees.description: Whether the measure agrees with the claim.
